chapter: Funerals, second lines and being an outsider
title: Band serenades an old man in a wheelchair
summary: Wood recounts a parade that stopped at a shotgun house to honour an elderly man, and the band not being invited to the lodge hall.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Turning my nose up at it. There was something that I did want to make sure I told you about and I don't remember whether I told you about this, recall this for you or not. But again, it's within this whole idea that the parades then were, uh, part of the life of the community. Yes. And there was an, an episode that I found just really interesting and also again moving, uh, there was a large parade and again, I don't know, I don't remember where they started or where they went to, but the band played for this group of men who were wearing their large regalia and the band, uh, you know, were, were dressed. I never saw a band that was really had fancy uniforms. They always just had black pants and a white shirt and a cap and stuff. But they, they, they, they marched down the street into the neighborhood and wherever it was that they were going, they were playing and everybody was enjoying playing. And all of a sudden they, they, they, uh, headed down this little narrow side street and, uh, couple of blocks and made a few turns and stopped in front of a modest little shotgun house, uh, and stood outside. And while some of the dignitaries of the large group went to the door and, and, and, and the people in the house came out and stood on the porch and brought out from inside the house and old man in a wheelchair. Mm-hmm. They rolled him out and sat him on the wheelchair on the front porch. And, you know, the band played a couple of numbers, serenaded him and, uh, he was old and frail, but obviously just loved the fact that, uh, he was being honored in that way. And his family felt honored and, uh, large, uh, people felt good that they had come and done that. And the musicians seemed to enjoy it too. And I was practically in tears standing on the sidewalk watching it all. But it was a very, uh, moving kind of thing that they did.
I've been involved in things like that. I agree.

Oh, yeah. And then, you know, they went back up to their regular parade route and went on down the street and ended up at the, uh, Lodge Hall where they were going to have some kind of meeting or party or what have you. And I don't believe, sometimes a band got to go in and have some refreshments and sometimes they didn't. And I believe on that day the band wasn't invited to come in and partake of the food and drink that the group was going to have.
Did you ever get invited in? And this is a good point to ask you about. No, I didn't. Uh, well, you saw.

And I don't think I would have gone, you know, I, don't know. If I had been invited, it would have been an insult not to accept the invitation. But I would have been pretty uneasy about it had I, you know, been in that situation. I guess I'm just as glad I didn't get invited.
Well, yeah. If, if, if they had a rest stop in somebody's yard where a beer was served, you wouldn't have gone into that.
Oh, probably. Yeah. That's kind of fun.
